Remote Work Scam UK: How to Spot a Fake Job Offer

A fee paid through a recruiter link or private account before you can verify a remote role is a serious scam warning.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-07 · Updated 2026-08-06 · 7 min read

Quick answer: A remote job offered entirely through chat, with no verifiable interview and a fee paid through a recruiter link or private account to start, is a scam warning. Verify genuine criminal-record checks independently. Refuse requests to route other people's money through your own account or repost parcels from your home. Report it to Report Fraud or Police Scotland on 101.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

What a fake remote-work offer looks like

This scam is an unsolicited message — often via WhatsApp, Telegram, or text — offering a highly-paid, minimal-effort remote job with no real application or interview process. An example of the style is: Congratulations! You've been selected for our remote data entry role — £35/hour, flexible hours. Reply to start onboarding today. A genuine employer should not hire you through chat messages alone without a verifiable process.

Why these offers are convincing

Remote work is now genuinely common, so an offer to work from home is not suspicious by itself. The warning is a fee to secure or unlock the job, a payment to a private account or unverified link, or a demand made before you can verify the employer and role.

For most individual applicants, agencies cannot charge for finding work. The main sector exception covers specified entertainment and creative occupations, photographic or fashion modelling, and professional sport; separate rules can apply to some incorporated work-seekers and publication-only services. Our recruitment agency scam guide sets out the rules in full. A genuine criminal-record check can carry a published fee, so the existence of a fee alone does not prove a scam.

Signs a remote job offer is a scam

  • You're hired with no real interview - contact is entirely through chat apps, with no call or verifiable meeting.
  • You're asked to pay a recruiter, private account or unverified link for training, equipment or a supposed criminal-record check before you can verify the employer, role, check level and official provider.
  • The 'job' asks you to take in, hold or pass on somebody else's money, or to accept and re-send parcels, using an account or address in your own name.
  • Contact happens only through a personal messaging app, not a company email domain.
  • The employer claims to be a UK limited company, but its name, company number, status, address or officers do not match Companies House — or its only online presence is the offer itself.

How the scam works step by step

First, an unsolicited message offers a remote role with unusually high pay for minimal effort, often with instant 'hiring' and no real interview. Second, you're asked to pay a fee for training, equipment, or a background check to 'start'. Third, in other versions, you're asked to receive money or packages and forward them elsewhere as part of your 'duties'. Either the upfront fee is simply stolen, or the forwarding task makes you an unwitting part of a wider fraud. If the role asks you to move someone else's money through an account in your name, that is the money-mule pattern.

Receiving and reposting parcels from your home is a separate reshipping or parcel-mule scam.

How to verify a remote job offer safely

If the employer claims to be a UK limited company, compare its legal name, company number, status, address and officers with Companies House. An absence or mismatch is a warning in that specific case. For other business structures, use the applicable register and independent contact details. Companies House registration is corroboration, not proof of the vacancy or contact. Apply again independently through the employer's own official careers page or domain, not a link in the message.

If a criminal-record check is mentioned, check which service and route actually apply. An individual can apply directly for a basic DBS check in England or Wales, a Level 1 disclosure in Scotland, or a basic AccessNI check in Northern Ireland; higher levels — including Level 2 and most PVG applications — are restricted to eligible roles and are started by an employer, organisation or registered body. Check the level, route and current fee on that service, not through a link a recruiter sent you.

  • Be wary of any 'job' that asks you to receive, hold, convert or forward someone else's money, or accept and forward parcels, through an account or address in your own name.
  • A genuine hiring process normally includes a real interview, not chat messages alone.

If you've already paid or acted on a fake job offer

If you paid a fee by card, contact your bank or card provider about a chargeback. A Section 75 claim may apply where the credit-card cash price was more than £100 and no more than £30,000.

If you sent a bank transfer, tell your bank the same day and ask about APP reimbursement: an eligible domestic consumer payment sent by Faster Payments or retail CHAPS on or after 7 October 2024 can be reimbursed up to £85,000, must be claimed within 13 months, is subject to exclusions, and may carry an excess of up to £100 that cannot be charged to a consumer the firm assesses as vulnerable — none of which makes a refund guaranteed.

If money passed through your account, stop, tell your bank immediately and follow the NCA's money-mule advice. If you only received or reposted parcels, stop accepting or forwarding them, preserve the records and get independent advice before handling anything else. If you shared bank or ID details, monitor your accounts and consider Cifas Protective Registration, which costs £30 and runs for two years, only where the exposure puts your identity at heightened risk; check Cifas's current criteria. Our scam recovery checklist sets out the order.

How to report a remote work scam (UK)

Report it to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland. For an SMS, forward the message to 7726. For WhatsApp, Telegram or Signal, preserve the evidence and use the app's report and block tools; 7726 is not the in-app reporting route. If the offer arrived by phishing email, forward it to report@phishing.gov.uk.

Frequently asked questions

Is genuine remote work common in the UK, or should I be suspicious of every offer?

Genuine remote work is widespread and not itself a warning sign. What matters is how you're hired: a fee demanded through a recruiter link or private account before you can verify the employer, or a request to route someone else's money through your own account, or unexplained parcel reshipping from your home, is the real tell - not the fact that a job is remote. A genuine criminal-record check is a separate matter and can carry a published fee.

Can a recruiter or employer legally charge me a fee to get a job?

Generally not. An agency cannot normally charge an individual work-seeker for finding work, and separate regulations apply in Great Britain and Northern Ireland; the main sector exception covers specified entertainment and creative occupations, photographic or fashion modelling, and professional sport. Our recruitment agency scam guide sets out the detail. A genuine criminal-record check is a different matter and can carry a published fee, so check the level, route and current fee on the relevant government service before paying anyone.

I've already sent money for training or equipment for a job I now think is fake — what do I do?

Contact your bank or card provider about a chargeback. A Section 75 claim may apply where the credit-card cash price was more than £100 and no more than £30,000. Stop all further contact, and report it to Report Fraud in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland. If you sent a bank transfer, tell your bank the same day and ask about APP reimbursement — our scam recovery checklist sets out the eligibility conditions, the cap, the claim window and the excess rules.

I received money into my account and forwarded it as part of a 'job' — am I in trouble?

Stop immediately and don't move any more money. Being asked to receive, hold, convert or forward someone else's money through your own account is money muling. Your bank may freeze or close accounts and the activity can be investigated, so tell your bank, keep records, and read the National Crime Agency's money-muling guidance before doing anything else. Our money mule scam guide covers this in more depth.

How do I report a fake remote job offer?

Report it to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland. Forward any phishing email to report@phishing.gov.uk.

  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
